denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CMG 0104 (inpatient rehabilitation facility admission, stroke) with dates of service 2026-09-12 through 2026-09-26. CARC 197: Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent. Payer remark: No authorization is on file. A retrospective medical necessity review may be requested with supporting clinical documentation within 60 days.

criteria.text: Requires active and ongoing intervention of at least two therapy disciplines, one of which is physical or occupational therapy.
Requires, and can reasonably be expected to actively participate in, an intensive rehabilitation program: generally at least 3 hours of therapy per day at least 5 days per week.
Reasonably expected to make measurable functional improvement of practical value within a prescribed period, documented against goals in an individualized plan of care.
Requires supervision by a rehabilitation physician with face-to-face visits at least 3 days per week to manage medical and rehabilitation needs.
The patient’s needs cannot be met at a less intensive level of care, such as a skilled nursing facility.

chart.text: Preadmission screening. 71 year old woman with an acute right middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke 4 days ago, NIHSS 8, dense left hemiparesis, left neglect, and oropharyngeal dysphagia on a modified diet. Needs PT for transfers and gait, OT for left upper extremity and self-care, and SLP for swallowing and cognition. Premorbidly independent, lives with her spouse in a single-level home. A skilled nursing facility would not provide the daily physician oversight she needs for the blood pressure lability and the dysphagia, nor three disciplines at this intensity. Recommend inpatient rehabilitation.

Admitted to inpatient rehabilitation from the acute hospital. History otherwise hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes. Medications reconciled. Code status full. Post-admission physician evaluation. Confirms the preadmission findings. Three disciplines ordered: PT, OT, and SLP, each to evaluate within 24 hours. She was sitting up at the edge of the bed with the acute PT and tolerated 45 minute sessions there without fatigue. I expect her to tolerate three hours a day. Prognosis for functional gains is good given premorbid independence and intact comprehension. Goals in 14 days: supervision level transfers, 150 feet with a hemi-walker, modified independent feeding, regular diet with thin liquids.
Social work met with the patient and her spouse to confirm the home address, the primary contact, and transportation for follow-up appointments. No barriers identified today.
PT evaluation. Transfers maximal assist of two, sit to stand with left knee buckling, unable to ambulate. Sitting balance fair, standing balance poor. Goals set, plan 5 to 6 days a week.
OT evaluation. left upper extremity flaccid with trace shoulder shrug, dependent for dressing and bathing, maximal assist for grooming, left neglect on cancellation testing. Goals set.

SLP evaluation. Oropharyngeal dysphagia with delayed swallow and throat clearing on thin liquids, mechanical soft and nectar thick recommended. Mild word-finding difficulty, follows two-step commands. Goals set.
Glucose checks before meals and at bedtime, ranging 130 to 224. Sliding scale given per protocol. Patient's own glucometer at bedside, sent home with family for safekeeping.

Rehab physician progress note, day 3, seen face to face. Blood pressure labile, 168 over 94 this morning, 112 over 70 last night with lightheadedness in therapy; adjusted the amlodipine timing. Dysphagia diet reviewed with SLP. left shoulder pain with range of motion, added a sling for transfers.
Daily weight 187 pounds, up 0 from yesterday. Intake and output recorded. Repositioned per schedule, skin checked.
Potassium 3.4 this morning, repleted with 20 milliequivalents oral per protocol. Recheck with morning labs.
Pharmacy note. Renal dosing reviewed, creatinine 1.1, no adjustments needed today. Home medication list reconciled with the daughter by phone, one duplicate statin removed.
Week one therapy minutes: PT 90, OT 75, SLP 45 daily, 210 minutes a day on 6 of 7 days. Tolerating sessions, asking for more, no sessions refused or cut short for fatigue.
Skin assessment on admission. Braden 19. Skin intact, no pressure injury, heels floated. Turn every two hours while in bed. Barrier cream to the sacrum as a precaution.

Team conference, day 7. Transfers improved from maximal assist of two to minimal assist of one. Gait 25 feet to 80 feet with a hemi-walker and contact guard. Swallow advanced to mechanical soft with nectar liquids. On track for the 14 day goals, continue.
Home levothyroxine resumed at the home dose this morning after review with the attending. No interactions flagged.
Chaplain visited at the patient's request, about twenty minutes. She appreciated the visit. No needs identified.
Patient requested something for sleep. Melatonin 5 milligrams given per order at 2130. Slept in two-hour stretches per night shift report.
IV site rotated from the left forearm to the right hand, old site without redness. Dressing dated. Patient tolerated well.
Dietitian consult. Regular diet with heart healthy modification. Intake about 60 percent of meals. Supplement shake twice daily added. Will follow.

Rehab physician progress note, day 10, seen face to face. Blood pressure steadier on the new schedule. Bladder scan residuals under 100, catheter out. Spasticity in the left hand, started a night splint. Reviewed therapy progress with the team.
Dentures labeled and placed in the denture cup at the bedside. Patient prefers them out at night. Oral care done.
Pneumococcal vaccine status reviewed, up to date per state registry. Influenza vaccine offered and accepted, given left deltoid.

Discharge summary, day 14. Transfers supervision, ambulating 160 feet with a hemi-walker and supervision, regular diet with thin liquids, feeding modified independent. Home with spouse, home health PT and OT arranged.
Fall risk assessment completed, score 48, high risk. Bed alarm on, nonskid socks, call light within reach, hourly rounding. Family at bedside this evening.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 197 denial can be answered from the record.
